title: LIBRA: Runtime Co-Tuning of Batch Size and Parallelism for Time-Efficient LLM Training
abstract: arXiv:2611.32008v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) requires choosing both a batch size and a parallel configuration. Existing systems make these decisions in isolation, tuning parallelism for throughput and batch size for convergence, but neither objective alone determines training efficiency. We present LIBRA, a lightweight runtime framework that co-tunes batch size and parallel configuration to minimize end-to-end time. LIBRA treats throughput and convergence as two noisy objectives and searches their joint space using parallel noisy expected hypervolume improvement (qNEHVI). To make this runtime search efficient, we propose hierarchical pruning, which removes infeasible and low-throughput parallel configurations through system-level performance estimation and then narrows batch-size candidates through critical-batch-size-aware convergence monitoring. translated_title: LIBRA：面向时间高效大语言模型训练的批大小与并行度运行时协同调优
translated_abstract: 摘要：训练大语言模型（LLM）需要同时选择批大小和并行配置。现有系统将这些决策割裂开来——为吞吐量调优并行度，为收敛性调优批大小——但仅凭其中任何一个目标都无法决定训练效率。我们提出LIBRA，一个轻量级的运行时框架，通过协同调优批大小和并行配置来最小化端到端训练时间。LIBRA将吞吐量和收敛性视为两个带噪声的目标，并使用并行噪声期望超体积改进（qNEHVI）在其联合空间中进行搜索。为了使这一运行时搜索高效，我们提出了层次化剪枝方法：首先通过系统级性能估计剔除不可行和低吞吐量的并行配置，然后通过基于临界批大小的收敛监测来缩小批大小候选范围。我们进一步设计了采集引导的并行评估，用以评估存续的候选配置……
tldr: LIBRA首次将批大小与并行配置协同调优，以qNEHVI多目标搜索为核心，结合层次化剪枝和采集引导的并行评估，实现最小化大语言模型训练端到端时间的轻量级运行时框架。
